=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- File: CLAUDE.md
  Line or code reference: lines 1971-1978 (post-change); specifically the line `PR #<n> merged — <no action needed | action needed>` on line 1972, and the line ``PR #<n> closed — decision needed` (with `#<issue> · ` in front when the PR has a source issue)` on lines 1973-1974.
  Problem: The §26.D terminal-report renames are documented inconsistently. The closed form gets the parenthetical `(with `#<issue> · ` in front when the PR has a source issue)`, but the merged form above it does not. Both forms are produced by the same `set_session_title` call at terminal report time, yet the spec only attaches the issue-prefix rule to one of them. The new `### Session titles` rule says every session title leads with the numbers, so an operator implementing §26.D literally would either (a) omit the prefix from the merged form (violating Session titles) or (b) add it (deviating from the literal text). The diff updated only the closed form.
  Why it fails at runtime: When a PR with a source issue merges, the pushing session renames itself to `PR #<n> merged — <no action needed | action needed>` without the `#<issue> · ` prefix that the rule mandates, so the operator cannot match the merged-report session to its issue from the first characters of the title. The PR description's done condition lists "report titles" (plural) gaining the prefix; the delivery covers only one of the two forms.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "`PR #<n> status check-in` unchanged; fixer and report titles prefixed" — PR description done-condition table, fifth row, citing CLAUDE.md §26.B steps 1b and 3, §26.C step 5, §26.D; also `agents.md` "stage-title sentence under the check-in loop" reference (per `docs/plans/issue-4886-numbered-session-titles-plan.md` goal 6) and the changelog fragment text "Merge report session renames ... when the PR has a source issue" implied by the new rule.
  Expected change site: CLAUDE.md §26.D, the `set_session_title` rename list that names both terminal forms (`PR #<n> merged — <no action needed | action needed>` and `PR #<n> closed — decision needed`), and the matching assertion in `tests/test_session_titles.py::test_claude_md_keeps_the_check_in_title_exact_and_prefixes_fixer_and_report`.
  Evidence of absence: The diff hunk at CLAUDE.md lines 1971-1978 inserts the parenthetical `(with `#<issue> · ` in front when the PR has a source issue)` only after the closed form. The merged form on the line above it has no analogous parenthetical. The new test asserts the closed form carries the prefix but contains no assertion that the merged form carries it, so the gap is not enforced. The PR description's done condition uses the plural "report titles" yet only one form is delivered; the `agents.md` "Numbers first in every title" sentence likewise scopes the rule to all stages but the §26.D spec contradicts it for the merged terminal report.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
